text:
Sam Yang: Quick question — Greenfield wants the POC to guarantee 99th p50 < 250ms for chat at 30 qps and an overflow plan if Dedicated pool bursts. How do we document the fallback behavior in the RFI and what pricing delta do we show?

Priya Patel: Short answer: fallback to hosted-compatible model variant with autoscale burst. Add a row in the capability matrix: 'Dedicated + burst to Hosted (model variant fallback)'. Note latency SLOs vary by seq len.

Sam Yang: Got it. They pushed back on 'fallback to hosted' for data residency. Any alternatives?

Marta Rivera: If they require no egress, we can use cross-tenant VPC peering to a customer-dedicated subnet (Private). For true air-gapped, on-prem package only. Mention both in RFP: "Private (VPC) option — no model data leaves tenant; On‑prem — fully air‑gapped."

Jordan Lee: For the RFI matrix, can we add columns: "Fallback mode", "Expected 99th latency (ms)", "Cost impact (delta %)"? They want clear numbers for procurement.

Priya Patel: Yep. Example numbers for their 30 qps chat workload (assume medium seq len): Dedicated alone = 99th ~220ms, Dedicated+burst-hosted = 99th ~300ms (depends on region). Cost delta: burst to hosted can add ~15-25% on unit cost during overflow windows.

FinOps Bot: Rough estimate: baseline monthly POC cost (Dedicated reserved 2x rtx6000 equiv): $18k. If bursts hit 10% of traffic to hosted, add ~ $3.2k. (Assumptions: token mix, avg seq 256 tok/session).

Sam Yang: Perfect — can you add that as an explicit cell in the RFI table? procurement wants worst-case monthly delta too.

Priya Patel: Will do. Also adding a short note on data residency: "When fallback occurs, inbound request metadata necessary for routing is retained in customer region; payloads are encrypted in transit; for customers requiring no egress, fallback is disabled by policy."

Marta Rivera: I attached the security questionnaire answers (see link) and uploaded a redacted network diagram to the RFP attachments. 

Sam Yang: Link? I need to attach to the RFI package.

Marta Rivera: https://files.redwood.internal/sales/greenfield/sec_q_answers_v3.pdf (redacted) — also added diagram: https://files.redwood.internal/sales/greenfield/network_v2.png :paperclip:

Jordan Lee: For the capability matrix row text suggestion: "Dedicated (primary) + Controlled Hosted Fallback (optional) — fallback only with customer opt-in, region-restricted, and auditable KMS keys; expected 99th latency increase 35-45% during overflow; cost delta estimate +15-25% on overflow traffic."

Sam Yang: Nice. Can you also give a short code snippet example for the routing policy to include in the technical appendix? procurement likes examples.

Priya Patel: Sure — minimal snippet below. Put in appendix as YAML.

Priya Patel: ```yaml
routing_policy: 
  primary: dedicated-cluster-greenfield
  fallback: hosted-variant-lowlatency
  fallback_conditions:
    - cluster_utilization > 0.85
    - observed_p99_latency > 250ms
  residency_constraints:
    - enforce_region: eu-west-1
    - disable_fallback_if_data_residency_required: true
  kms: customer_managed_key
```

Sam Yang: Sweet. One more ask — they want a single-line phrasing for the RFI describing SLAs during POC. Any suggestions?

Jordan Lee: "During the POC, Redwood will maintain a 99.5% availability SLO for Dedicated capacity; latency targets are workload-dependent and documented per workload profile; controlled fallback may increase latency and costs as listed in the pricing appendix."

Marta Rivera: Also flagged a legal question re: liability if fallback exposes data outside region. Legal asked for exact wording; recommend: "Fallback disabled until customer signs the controlled-fallback addendum."

Sam Yang: OK thanks — I'll fold these into the RFI and re-upload. Planning to send to Greenfield by EOD. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment for hosted-variant-lowlatency scheduled 2024-11-02 09:00 UTC — no expected downtime.

Sam Yang: Thanks all. I updated the draft in the RFP folder and linked the attachments. Moving to final review. :rocket:
